figure.name: Karl Marx
figure.role: Critic of capitalism, class power, exploitation, and historical economic systems.
figure.hook: Marx = class struggle and capitalism as a historical system.
whyHere: Marx belongs here because he gives the socialism road its central pressure point: capitalism is not only buying and selling, but a historical system of class power.
That matters because later socialist, communist, social-democratic, labor, and anti-communist arguments all react to Marx, whether they follow him, revise him, or reject him.
figure.cleanIdea: To understand modern politics, ask who owns productive property, who sells labor, who receives profit, and how that relationship shapes power.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: A radical critique of class power turns into one of the most influential political texts in history.

ideas.title: Class Struggle
ideas.plainDefinition: Class struggle means conflict between social classes over work, property, power, law, and who receives the value society creates.
ideas.context: In the Marx path, class struggle is not just disagreement. It is the engine of political conflict inside class society.
ideas.whyMatters: Class struggle matters because it turns socialism from a vague wish for fairness into a question about power: who owns, who works, who governs, and who benefits.

sources.title: Manifesto of the Communist Party / Part I

ideas.title: Surplus Value
ideas.plainDefinition: Surplus value is the Marxist idea that workers create more value than they receive back in wages, and that the difference can become profit.
ideas.context: In the Marx path, surplus value is one way to explain exploitation without reducing it to personal cruelty.
ideas.whyMatters: Surplus value matters because it asks where profit comes from and why wage labor can look free while still producing dependency and class power.

sources.title: Capital, Volume I / Marxists Internet Archive

ideas.title: Means of Production
ideas.plainDefinition: Means of production are the land, tools, machines, factories, infrastructure, and resources used to produce goods and services.
ideas.context: In the Marx path, the key question is not only who works, but who controls the productive property that work depends on.
ideas.whyMatters: Means of production matters because it separates personal belongings from productive property. Many socialism arguments are really about who controls production, not whether anyone owns a toothbrush.
